title: Per-chunk telemetry, trace correlation, and redaction for streaming API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add per-chunk telemetry, deterministic trace/span correlation, and safe redaction for streamed content across the Core API (streaming responses for generation, tool/function calling, and structured output flows). This ticket covers the data model, runtime hooks, metrics & logs schema, compatibility layer for older SDKs that only expect final responses, and a rollout with feature gating.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics emitted per streamed chunk including size_bytes, token_count, chunk_latency_ms, upstream_queue_ms, and kv_cache_hit (true/false)
Tracing spans created/ended for each chunk with a stable chunk_id correlated to request_id and parent span; spans propagated through function/tool calls and to external tool integrations

All streamed text and structured payload fields that may contain PII are redacted in logs and non-encrypted metrics payloads according to the redaction config; raw full content only stored in encrypted traces if retention is required and allowed
Backward compatibility: SDKs that do not support per-chunk events still receive full final payload and no client-facing behavior change
End-to-end tests demonstrating observability for streaming generation with function/tool calling and a sample structured output schema
Dashboard panels in Console showing chunk distribution, tail latencies, and KV cache effectiveness for streaming endpoints
engineering_notes: Initial spike showed ~12% p99 tail improvement when using chunk-level queue metrics to tune batching windows
Trade-off: emitting per-chunk metrics increases cardinality — we will sample at 1/10 for free-tier and 100% for enterprise by default; knobs exposed on Dedicated/Private
To avoid downstream cardinality explosions, use normalized label values (hardware_family, model_variant) and avoid embedding prompt text in labels
Span correlation will use a stable chunk_id (<request_id>-cNN) so older tracing backends can stitch chunks without schema changes
Redaction uses configurable pattern lists + structured-schema rules; default rules redact tokens matching email, SSN, and credit card patterns in streamed logs/metrics
test_plan: Unit tests for metric emitter: validate metric fields, label normalization, and sampling behavior
Integration test: simulate streaming generation with a function call that returns sensitive fields — verify redaction in logs and masked values in console
Tracing test: assert span timeline for chunks and that chunk_id ties to parent request span; test propagation through a mock tool endpoint
Compatibility test: SDK v0 (no chunk events) receives final assembled response; SDK v1 (chunk-aware) receives chunked events and correlates them to same request_id
Load test: 2000 concurrent streaming connections measuring additional metric backfill storage and tracing throughput
rollout_plan: Feature-flag behind 'stream_chunk_observability' default off for free accounts
Enable 10% of hosted traffic for two days, monitor error rates and metric cardinality
Increase to 50% and enable sampling controls if backend costs are stable
Enable for Dedicated customers by default with per-tenant sampling config; Private deployments include toggle in admin console
Post-rollout: run a 72-hour monitoring sweep and publish runbook for on-call to revert if trace backend saturates
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: metric cardinality blow-up -> Mitigation: label normalization, default sampling, and per-tenant caps
Risk: exposing PII in logs/metrics -> Mitigation: strict redaction rules, encrypted traces for raw payloads with KMS access control
Risk: increased latency from additional bookkeeping -> Mitigation: async emitters, non-blocking tracing hooks, and micro-batching of metric exports
monitoring_queries: sql: SELECT count(*) FROM traces WHERE chunk_id IS NOT NULL AND created_at >= now() - interval '1 day'
